intro: An affine quantizer can place real zero away from integer zero. Separating scale and zero point reveals how rounding and saturation change reconstructed values.
task: Map real values to signed 8-bit codes and reconstruct them, inspecting zero points, ties-to-even rounding, and saturation.
requirements: values is any finite numeric array; scale is a strictly positive real scalar; zero_point is an integer in [-128,127]. Require abs(values/scale)<=1e30.
Compute q=clip(rint(values/scale)+zero_point,-128,127), where rint rounds ties to the nearest even integer. Return q as np.int8.
Return dict quantized and reconstructed, with reconstructed=(q-zero_point)*scale as float64. Subtract the zero point after promoting q to a wider dtype.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Round before adding the offset
hints.body: The zero point maps real zero exactly to its chosen integer code.

hints.title: Avoid int8 subtraction overflow
hints.body: Convert quantized codes to float64 before subtracting the zero point.

explanation: Affine quantization separates the spacing between representable real values from the integer code assigned to real zero. This supports asymmetric real ranges.

Saturation is distinct from rounding error: once a value crosses the representable range, changing it further leaves its integer code fixed. The lesson uses supplied calibration parameters rather than fitting them.
